newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar opens flat on quiet overseas trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar opens flat on quiet overseas trade.

text.p: Canada's dollar opened flat in light trading on Monday at C$1.3974 (US$0.7156) after a quiet overnight session on overseas markets, traders said.
They said there was likely to be another test of the dollar's weakness with a possible move to the C$1.4010 level as investors continue to keep an eye on U.S. interest rates.
"You've got to figure after last week that we'll take another run at it," one trader said.
The Canada dollar weakened to C$1.3974 on Friday -- its lowest point in two years -- after the U.S. government reported a jump in the core producer price index for March.
The core producer price index rose 0.4 percent, compared to market expectations of a 0.1 percent rise.
Traders said the U.S. economic data increased market speculation that inflationary pressures persist in the U.S. economy and could prompt the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise rates.

"What I'm hearing is that people are talking about even more than one Fed hike," said Reid Farrill, adviser for corporate foreign exchange with CIBC Wood Gundy. "If that's going to be worked into the market, I don't see C$1.4000 (US$0.7142) as being the bottom for the Canadian dollar."

A 25-basis-point rate hike by the Fed on March 25 widened the spread between U.S. and Canadian short-term rates to more than 200 points, pressuring the Canadian dollar and renewing calls for the Bank of Canada to follow suit.
Canada's dollar has shed almost four percent of its value against the U.S. dollar since January.
Analysts said the Canada unit would continue to drift in a weak range as investors kept a wary eye on U.S. data for signs of creeping inflation.
The U.S. consumer price index, due to be released on Tuesday, will be the next big number to look at, Farrill said.
The Canada dollar could also suffer if stock markets continue to slide, making intervention by the Bank of Canada possible near the C$1.4010 (US$0.7137) level.
The bank could be stepping into the market ahead of schedule as it did last week, one trader said.
The Bank of Canada intervened to support a flagging Canada dollar on Thursday and Friday.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar was flat at 1.2308 marks compared to Friday's close of 1.2311 marks and was unchanged at 90.20 yen from Friday's 90.20 yen.
